title: N4, processes and scheduling, is met
description: Processes, the scheduler, signals, terminals, the clock and the arm64 trap and system-call entry now live in the safe kernel crate and in hal.
content:
Milestone N4 closed on 2026-10-24, tagged [`n4-processes`]({{ site.repo }}/releases/tag/n4-processes). In seventeen slices, from 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-24, processes and scheduling left the LandingZone tree:

- **Into the `kernel` crate**, which the compiler refuses to build with any `unsafe`: timeouts and tasks, processes, credentials, fork and exit, resource limits and accounting, the file descriptors, kqueue, select and poll, signals, futex, the scheduler, sysctl's core, the message buffer, terminals and pseudo-terminals, the timecounters and the clock.
- **Into `hal`**, the only crate allowed `unsafe`, each site with a written proof: the context switch, spl and soft interrupts, the kernel lock, arm64's timer, exception vectors, trap and system-call entry, the user copies, signal delivery, the Spectre-BHB trampolines and kernel page-table isolation.

105 of the 331 system calls are now handled natively, from 17 when N4 started. The whole test suite passed on arm64, on two and on four CPUs, with the installer end to end, and the comparison with a real OpenBSD found no new difference.

The cost is measured too: under QEMU on arm64, the page fault is 41 % slower than at N3, pipe 35 %, fork plus exec 24 %, fork plus exit 19 %, a file read 11 %. Correctness comes first; those numbers go to N12, the performance milestone.

Next is N5: the VFS and the file systems. The [Status]({{ '/status/' | relative_url }}) page has the details.

title: The repositories move to the EmiBSD organisation
description: EmiBSD.LZ is now LandingZone, the native system is now Kernel, both under github.com/EmiBSD.
content:
EmiBSD's code now lives in its own GitHub organisation, [github.com/EmiBSD](https://github.com/EmiBSD), under new names:

- **[LandingZone]({{ site.repo_lz }})**, formerly EmiBSD.LZ: the file-by-file port of the OpenBSD kernel to Rust.
- **[Kernel]({{ site.repo }})**: the redesign of that port, the system this site describes.

GitHub redirects the old URLs. Nothing else changed: the history, the milestones and the LandingZone commit that Kernel is synced to are the same.

On the same day Kernel merged N4.5a: the context switch, the per-CPU core and the scheduler lock moved into `hal`, and the sleep and run queues, the idle loop, the priorities and kernel threads into the `kernel` crate. The [Status]({{ '/status/' | relative_url }}) page has the new numbers.

title: A new site for EmiBSD
description: www.emibsd.org now explains the project, the process and its status in a few pages.
content:
The single landing page that used to live at emibsd.org is now a small site:

- [About]({{ '/about/' | relative_url }}): why EmiBSD exists and how it relates to OpenBSD.
- [Process]({{ '/process/' | relative_url }}): from the 1:1 port in LandingZone to the redesign in Kernel, and the agents that do the work.
- [Status]({{ '/status/' | relative_url }}): every kernel subsystem, moved, in progress or pending.
- [Docs]({{ '/docs/' | relative_url }}): building, booting in QEMU and the layout of the tree.
- [Contributing]({{ '/contributing/' | relative_url }}): issues, target hardware and a FAQ.

Where things stand today: milestones N0 to N3 are met. Memory management (uvm) now lives in the `kernel` crate, which the compiler refuses to build with any `unsafe`. N4, processes and scheduling, is under way: timeouts, processes and credentials, file descriptors, kqueue, select(2) and poll(2) have moved; the scheduler is next. 44 of the 331 entries of the system-call table are now handled natively by the `abi` module.

EmiBSD is pre-alpha and runs only in QEMU. There is no release yet.
